tutorialTgSteps: Search for @BotFather in Telegram and open the chat
Send /newbot and follow the prompts to set a name and username
BotFather will reply with a Bot Token (like 123456:ABC-DEF...)
Paste the Token into the input field above and turn on the switch
Find your Bot in Telegram and send a message to test it

tutorialFsSteps: Go to open.feishu.cn, log in and open the Developer Console
Click "Create Enterprise Custom App", fill in the app name and description
On the "Credentials & Basic Info" page, copy the App ID and App Secret
Find "Add App Capabilities" in the left menu, add "Bot" capability and give it a name
Go to "Permissions", search and enable im:message (send and receive messages)
Go to "Events & Callbacks" → "Event Configuration", change to "Receive events via long connection"
Important: Go to "Version Management", create and publish a version first (long connection config requires a published app)
Paste the App ID and App Secret into the input fields above and turn on the switch

webSearch.label: Web Search
webSearch.description: Search the internet for real-time information. Use when you need the latest news, technical docs, current events, or any external knowledge not in memory.
webSearch.maxResultsDesc: Number of results to return, default 10

webFetch.label: Fetch Web Page
webFetch.description: Fetch the content of a given URL and extract text. Useful for reading articles, docs, API responses, etc. Pair with web_search: first search to find a URL, then use web_fetch to read the full content.

browser.label: Browser
browser.description: Control a headless browser (navigate, click, type, scroll, screenshot, evaluate JS). Use the action parameter to pick an operation; see its description for per-action parameters. Element [ref] ids from snapshot become stale after any navigate/click/type — those operations auto-return a fresh snapshot, always use refs from the latest one.
browser.actionDesc: Which operation to run. Required params per action: navigate→url; click→ref; type→text (optional ref, pressEnter); scroll→direction (optional amount); select→ref+value; key→key; wait→(optional timeout, state); evaluate→expression. start, stop, snapshot, screenshot, show take no extra params.
browser.keyDesc: Key name (required for key), e.g. Enter, Escape, Tab, Control+a
browser.timeoutDesc: Timeout in milliseconds (optional for wait, default 5000)
browser.stateDesc: Wait state (optional for wait): domcontentloaded / idle
browser.pressEnterDesc: Press Enter after typing (optional for type)

channel.label: Channel
channel.description:
Manage channel messages (for broadcasts and group discussions).
Actions:
- read(channel, count?): View recent messages in a channel
- post(channel, content): Send a message to a channel
- create(name, members, intro?): Create a new channel
- list: View channels you have joined
Note: For one-on-one messaging with an agent, use the dm tool instead of simulating a private chat via channels.
channel.countDesc: Number of messages to read (optional for read, default 20)

artifact.label: Create Preview
artifact.description:
Call this tool when you need to show the user an HTML page, code snippet, or long-form Markdown content.
Content is rendered in a standalone preview panel where the user can view results in real time.
Good for: runnable HTML/CSS/JS pages, interactive visualizations, SVG charts, complete code files, long formatted documents.
Not for: short text replies, conversational answers, one-line code snippets (just show those inline).
artifact.typeDesc: Content type: html (rendered page), code (syntax highlighted), markdown (document)
artifact.titleDesc: Display title, a short description of the content
artifact.contentDesc: Full content (HTML source / code / Markdown text)
artifact.languageDesc: Programming language (only for type=code), e.g. javascript, python, css

dm.label: Direct Message
dm.description:
Send a single direct message to another agent to inform them of something.
Do not use this tool to assign tasks or get results; that is subagent's job.

cron.label: Scheduled Tasks
cron.description:
Create and manage scheduled tasks. Scheduled tasks run automatically in the background, spawning an independent session to execute the specified prompt when triggered.
Actions:
- list: View all tasks
- add(scheduleType, schedule, prompt, label?, model?): Create a task
  - scheduleType "at": One-time, schedule is an ISO time string
  - scheduleType "every": Interval, schedule is minutes (e.g. 60 = hourly)
  - scheduleType "cron": Cron expression (e.g. "0 7 * * *" = every day at 7 AM)
  - model: Optional, specify the model for task execution (defaults to the chat model)
- remove(id): Delete a task
- toggle(id): Enable/disable a task
cron.scheduleDesc: Schedule: ISO time (at), minutes (every, e.g. 60=hourly), cron expression (cron)
cron.promptDesc: Prompt to execute when triggered (required for add)
cron.modelDesc: Specify execution model (optional, defaults to the chat model)

notify.label: Notification
notify.description:
Send a system notification (desktop popup) to the user.
Use cases:
- The user says 'remind me about xxx', 'notify me when...', 'don't let me forget xxx'
- A scheduled task prompt explicitly includes notification intent
- A monitoring/scheduled task discovers something requiring user attention
If everything is normal with no issues, do not call this tool.

todoWrite.label: Todo
todoWrite.description:
Manage the todo list for the current session. Pass the complete todos array each call to replace the current state (replacement style).
Each todo needs:
- content: static description (e.g. 'Read spec')
- activeForm: in-progress description (e.g. 'Reading spec')
- status: pending | in_progress | completed
Convention: at most one in_progress at a time.
todoWrite.activeFormDesc: In-progress form description (shown in UI while in_progress)
todoWrite.todosDesc: Complete todo list; each call replaces the previous list

pinnedMemory.pinDescription: Save an item to pinned memory. Use when the user says 'remember this', 'note this down', 'don't forget this later'. Pinned memories are always kept in context.
pinnedMemory.unpinDescription: Remove an item from pinned memory. Use when the user says 'forget xxx' or 'delete this memory'. Supports fuzzy matching: any line containing the keyword you provide will be removed.
pinnedMemory.unpinKeywordDesc: Keyword of the memory to remove, matched fuzzily

experience.recallDescription: Browse the experience library. Without parameters, returns an overview of all categories. With a category name, returns specific experiences in that category. When the user asks you to do a concrete task (write code, research, create documents, analyze problems, etc.), check this tool first for relevant experience before starting. Not needed for casual chat, Q&A, or everyday conversation.
experience.recallCategoryDesc: Category name. Omit to get an overview of all categories
experience.recordDescription: Record a lesson learned to the experience library. Use when: the user points out a mistake and explains the correct approach, you discover an effective method after trying multiple approaches, or the user explicitly says 'from now on do/don't do this'. Each entry should be concise and direct, one sentence.
experience.recordCategoryDesc: Category for the experience, a 2-4 word phrase, e.g. 'tool usage', 'search tips', 'response style'
experience.recordContentDesc: The specific experience content, concise and direct, one sentence

outputFile.label: Stage Files
outputFile.description: After successfully creating files for anyone (users, agents), or when asked to provide a file, call this tool to present them in the conversation so the user can click to open. Only call when the file exists; do not call if the file is missing or creation failed. Don't just mention file paths in text — call this tool.
outputFile.filepathsDesc: Array of absolute file paths to stage
outputFile.labelDesc: (Compat) File name shown to the user

wait.label: Wait
wait.description: Wait for a specified number of seconds. Used to keep the turn active while waiting for background tasks to complete.

subagent.label: Launch Sub-agent
subagent.description: Create a continuable sub-agent instance for a delegated task. Returns immediately with taskId and threadId; results are delivered back in the background. Use agent to target an agent, or agent="?" to list agents.
subagent.taskDesc: Complete instructions and required context for the subagent. The subagent cannot see the current conversation history unless you include it here.
subagent.agentDesc: Target agent id from the team roster, using the value shown in backticks. Choose the agent whose persona, strengths, and model best fit the task; the roster shows each model and summary. Omit for the current agent; pass "?" to list agents.
subagent.labelDesc: Optional display label, such as "research 1" or "draft 2". Display-only; resume by passing the returned threadId to subagent_reply.
subagent.instanceDesc: Legacy field, accepted only as label compatibility. New calls should use label; resume with threadId.
subagent.accessDesc: Optional permission tier: "read" for read-only research, exploration, or review; "write" for execution, edits, or commands. Omit to inherit the current session permission.
subagent.modelDesc: Optional model override as provider/id. Omit to use the target agent's configured chat model.
subagent.includeSessionFilesDesc: Optional. When true, the sub-agent may read attachments and resource files registered in the current session. Default: false.

installSkill.label: Install Skill
installSkill.description: Install a new skill for yourself. Mode A: Provide a GitHub repo URL (containing SKILL.md) to auto-fetch and install. Mode B: Directly provide skill_content + skill_name, for self-authored skills. The skill takes effect immediately after installation.
installSkill.reasonDesc: Explain why this skill is needed (for audit, required)
installSkill.userRequestedDesc: Whether the user explicitly requested installation (true = user skill, false = learned skill)

updateSettings.label: Settings
updateSettings.description:
Modify Codia's settings. Two actions available:
- search + query: Search settings by keyword, see current values and options
- apply + key + value: Change a setting (requires user confirmation)

If you already know the exact key, you can apply directly.
updateSettings.actionDesc: Action: search to find settings / apply to change a setting
updateSettings.searchNoResults: No settings matching "{query}". Try a broader keyword.
updateSettings.searchMissingQuery: The search action requires a query parameter.
updateSettings.applyMissingParams: The apply action requires both key and value parameters.
updateSettings.bridgeMediaPublicBaseUrlDesc: Public HTTP(S) base URL used when bridge adapters need to deliver locally staged media files.
updateSettings.computerUseDesc: Enable or disable the experimental computer control switch under Settings > Experiments. When enabled, new conversations expose it to the primary Agent; when disabled, new conversations cannot see it and frozen old conversations are rejected if they call it.
updateSettings.memoryFactsDesc: Edit the current Agent's trusted memory facts when editable memory is enabled.
updateSettings.memoryFactsDisabled: Editable memory facts are disabled. Enable the memory.editable_facts experiment first.
updateSettings.experienceDesc: Enable/disable experience recall and recording for current Agent
updateSettings.sandboxNetworkDesc: Allow sandboxed commands to access the public internet; commands are already unrestricted by Codia networking when the sandbox is off

stopTask.label: Stop background task
stopTask.description: Stop a running background task. Pass the task_id to terminate it. Supported task types include sub-agent tasks, image/video generation tasks, etc.

subagentReply.label: Continue Sub-agent
subagentReply.description: Append a task to an open sub-agent instance in the current session. Use current_status with subagents first to see available threadIds.
subagentReply.threadIdDesc: The threadId of the sub-agent instance to continue. It must be an open subagent instance in the current session.
subagentReply.taskDesc: Complete instructions and required context to append to that sub-agent.
subagentReply.accessDesc: Optional permission tier: "read" or "write". Omit to reuse the instance access, still bounded by the current session permission.

subagentClose.label: Close Sub-agent
subagentClose.description: Close a no-longer-needed sub-agent instance in the current session and free a continuable instance slot.
subagentClose.threadIdDesc: The threadId of the open sub-agent instance to close.
subagentClose.reasonDesc: Optional closing reason, saved as the instance's final summary.

workflow.label: Workflow
workflow.description: Orchestrate multiple sub-agents with a deterministic JS script (agent/parallel/pipeline/workflow). Use for controlled fan-out, staged analysis, and synthesizing results from multiple child agents. The tool returns a task id immediately and completes in the background; resumeFromRunId can replay completed agent nodes from a prior compatible workflow journal.
workflow.scriptDesc: Workflow JavaScript source beginning with export const meta = {...}.
workflow.argsDesc: Optional value exposed to the workflow as args.
workflow.resumeFromRunIdDesc: Previous workflow runId (taskId) to resume from; unchanged completed agent nodes are replayed from the journal.

beautify.coverStyleGuide:
Default Markdown cover visual guidelines:

1. Art direction: modern institutional editorial design that feels clear, restrained, and credible; prefer authentic photography, abstract geometry, data, or collaboration scenes instead of anime key art by default.
2. Color: build from cool white, graphite, and low-saturation teal; use accent color sparingly and preserve strong title contrast.
3. Composition: follow a clear grid and information hierarchy, keep generous whitespace, and avoid piles of floating symbols.
4. Content: extract one core idea from the article and express it through a scene, structure, or object rather than illustrating the summary word for word.
5. Material: use clean digital surfaces by default; do not make rice paper, vintage print, warm yellow paper, or heavy grain the shared motif.
6. Narrative: ground imagery in collaboration, research, engineering, or decision-making; avoid unmotivated fantasy and decorative sentimentality.
7. Adaptation: light mode uses a cool white base with dark text; dark mode uses graphite with restrained highlights. Both must remain readable.
8. Output: default to landscape 3:2; use a close landscape ratio only when the provider cannot produce 3:2, and never stretch the image.

themeTone.dark: Dark theme: low illumination, restrained highlights, dark areas still preserving paper fiber and material layers.
themeTone.light: Light theme: soft warm light, low contrast, clean whitespace, visible paper fiber.
